text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- The Swiss government presented a plan for Alpine crossing fees aimed at limiting the number of heavy trucks crossing the Alps to 650,000 by the year 2001.

- The death penalty will become an issue again in Switzerland if a youth faction of the right wing Swiss People's Party follow plans to launch a public referendum to re-introduce capital punishment in Switzerland. The proponents need 100,000 signatures to force a referendum.
- Beat Curty and its cash and carry chain Prodega plan to cooperate with Metro, Europe's largest retailing group.
- The Swiss government plans to introduce new constitutional guidlines for organ transplants in Switzerland along with measures to ban unethical organ trading.
- The Swiss parliamentary justice commission has drafted a law which would allow abortions within the first 14 weeks of pregnancy.
